name: BALOOT

content.text: Baloot is the quintessential card game of Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, a high-strategy trick-taking contest derived from the French Belote. Played by four players in partnerships, it revolves around two primary contracts: 'Sun' (No-Trump) and 'Hokom' (Trump). The game is famous for its complex card values that shift based on the contract, and for 'Projects'â€”valued combinations like sequences and four-of-a-kinds. It is not just a game but a cultural institution, demanding intense concentration and partnership signaling.

Brought to the Arabian Peninsula by French influence or via merchants in the early 20th century. While it shares the DNA of Belote, it was heavily adapted to local tastes, particularly with the introduction of the 'Sun' contract and the doubling of scores.
32-card pack. Remove cards 2-6 from a standard 52-card deck.

Dealer gives 3 cards to each player, then 2. The next card is turned face up. Players then bid to take the contract (Hokom/Sun or Pass). Once a contract is chosen, the dealer finishes the deal so everyone has 8 cards.

items.text: Kahwa Variation: Includes more detailed doubling rules where the score can be multiplied up to four times.
